exemplars.label: Correlation-ID + secret hygiene (closest current instance)
exemplars.note: Bespoke trace-id propagation + the "never capture Authorization headers or bodies" hygiene. Pre-structlog (migrate per ADR-0006), but the correlation-id + secret-hygiene patterns are the seed to imitate.

exemplars.label: Canonical structlog + uvicorn + JSON setup (reference)
exemplars.note: The reference structlog + uvicorn + JSON-to-stdout config to adapt into setup_logging(). Pair with asgi-correlation-id for request ids.

road.decided_approach: structlog + asgi-correlation-id (Python) / pino (TS). Structured JSON to stdout, a correlation id per request, never swallow exceptions or log secrets, generic errors to clients with detail in the logs. Build on Contacts' secret hygiene + agent-sites' generic-error convention. 9 rules recorded; see ADR-0006.
road.name: Error handling & structured logging
road.summary: How we handle errors and emit structured logs.
road.validation_note: Mechanical survey 2026-06-30 across ~/Projects: no shared logging pattern (all plain-text/ad-hoc; 3+ repos swallow exceptions; only Contacts has a bespoke correlation id). Greenfield decision — no entrenched standard to dislodge.

check.hint: structlog JSONRenderer to stdout in prod; ConsoleRenderer in dev

rules.reason: 12-factor: Coolify/Docker capture stdout and the portfolio's log aggregation expects machine-parseable JSON. File logging fragments and is lost on container restart.
rules.rule: Emit structured JSON logs to stdout (not files) in production; pretty console output in dev.

check.hint: no Authorization/token/password/body fields in log calls

rules.reason: Logs are aggregated and retained; a secret in a log is a leaked secret. Contacts already enforces 'never capture Authorization headers or bodies' — make it portfolio-wide.
rules.rule: Never log secrets, credentials, auth headers, tokens, or full request bodies. Redact or omit.

check.note: also flag empty TS catch blocks

rules.reason: Silent swallows hide failures (found in 3+ repos in the survey). An error you can't see is an outage you learn about from users.
rules.rule: Never silently swallow an exception. A deliberate swallow must carry an inline justification AND log the error; bare `except Exception: pass` (Python) or empty `catch {}` (TS) is forbidden.

rules.reason: Bare print/console output isn't structured, leveled, or captured consistently; it bypasses the logging pipeline.
rules.rule: Use the configured logger; no bare `print()` (Python) or `console.log` (TS) in application (non-test, non-script) code.

rules.reason: A stack trace without the request id and the entity ids is hard to act on. Structured fields are queryable in aggregation.
rules.rule: Log exceptions with context — `logger.exception(...)` / bound structured fields, including the correlation id and relevant identifiers — not a bare string.

rules.reason: Prevents information leakage and gives users a clean message; agent-sites already does this (`{ error: 'Database error' }, 500`).
rules.rule: Return a generic error message + status to the client; put the diagnostic detail in the logs. Never leak internals/stack traces to clients.

rules.reason: Correlation ids let you trace one request across all its log lines and services; without them, multi-step failures are guesswork.
rules.rule: Attach a correlation/request id to every request and include it in every log line for that request (Python: `asgi-correlation-id` + structlog contextvars).

rules.reason: One library per ecosystem keeps logging consistent and portable across the portfolio's many services.
rules.rule: Structured logging library: Python → `structlog`; TS server → `pino`. Don't introduce alternatives (loguru/winston/etc.).

rules.reason: No TS app currently has an error boundary — an unhandled render error white-screens the user instead of degrading gracefully.
rules.rule: Every Next.js app ships an `error.tsx`/`global-error.tsx` and a React error boundary; client errors render a generic message.
